ApiError.description: A refusal: what kind, and the sentence a person would be shown.

AppliedFilter.description:
One applied audio filter or video effect: a catalogue id plus whatever
parameters were set. The catalogues themselves (and the FFmpeg strings
they build) live in the UI today; the model only stores the numbers.

enabled.description: False bypasses without losing settings. Absent means enabled.

id.description:
Which catalogue entry this is, e.g. "sepia". Not minted; an id the
catalogue no longer knows is simply skipped at render time.

keys.description:
The knobs that ride rather than hold: a sorted run of keys per
parameter name, each `at` a fraction of the clip like a `ClipKey`'s.
A parameter with keys is played from them and its `params` entry is
only what it falls back to with the keys taken off.

params.description:
The user's knob settings, keyed by parameter name. Missing keys mean
the catalogue's defaults; ordered so serialisation is stable.

AudioStreamInfo.description: An audio stream, as the UI sees it.

language.description: The stream's language tag, or empty.

title.description: The name the file gives the stream, or empty.

index.description: The stream's index within the file - what [`Clip::audio_stream`] holds.

language.description: The track's language tag, e.g. "eng"; empty when unstated.

title.description:
The name the file gives the track, when it gives one ("Desktop
Audio", "Mic/Aux"); empty otherwise, and the UI numbers it.

Background.description:
What fills the frame where the picture does not reach: the bars either
side of a wide shot in a tall frame, or the margin round a picture
scaled down. Nothing - black, as every project was before there was a
choice - a blurred, enlarged copy of the clip's own frame, a colour, or
a still from the bin.

A timeline carries one ([`Timeline::background`]) and a clip may carry
its own over it ([`Clip::background`]); which clips have one at all is
[`Timeline::background_of`]'s to say.

oneOf.description: Black: nothing drawn behind the picture.
The clip's own frame, enlarged to cover the whole frame and blurred.

amount.description:
How soft, `0..=1`: a blur of a twelfth of the frame's shorter
side at one.

oneOf.description: One flat colour, `#rrggbb`.

color.description: The colour, as a title's colours are written.

oneOf.description: A still from the bin, enlarged to cover the frame.

mediaId.description: The bin item. One that has gone, or none yet, draws nothing.

BrushTool.description: The four brushes of a custom cutout.

oneOf.description: Keeps what the model thought might be the subject under the stroke.
Keeps everything under the stroke.
Removes what the model was unsure of under the stroke.
Removes everything under the stroke.

Clip.description:
One placed piece of a timeline: a stretch of media (or a title) with its
timing, mix, transform, and effects. Everything an edit decision touches
lives here, which is why most commands are clip commands.

audioStream.description:
Which of the media's audio streams this clip plays, by the stream's
index in the file - see [`MediaItem::audio_tracks`]. None is the first
in file order, which is every clip from before files with several
were told apart and every clip of a file with one.

background.description:
What fills the frame behind this clip's picture, over the
timeline's [`Timeline::background`]: None follows the timeline's,
and `Some(Background::None)` is black under a timeline that has one.
Only a picture on the lowest picture lane has a background at all;
see [`Timeline::background_of`].

blend.description:
How the picture's colour meets what is beneath it: "normal",
"multiply", "screen", "add", "lighten", "darken".

crop.description:
What is cut off each edge of the source before it is fitted, as
fractions of the source's width and height.

cutout.description:
The background taken away by a mask rather than a key colour; see
[`Cutout`]. Keying by colour is a package on `video_effects`.

detachedFrom.description: On a detached audio clip: the video clip the sound came from.

duration.description:
Seconds of timeline the clip occupies. Source seconds divided by
`speed`; never below a sixtieth of a second.

enhanced.description:
The clip's Enhance: the media it was cut from and the enhanced copy
of it, and which of the two it shows. Absent until Enhance has made
a copy; switching it off shows the original again without running
the model a second time.

fadeIn.description: Seconds of audio ramp-in from silence at the head. Zero for none.

fadeOut.description: Seconds of audio ramp-out to silence at the tail. Zero for none.

filters.description:
Audio filters, in order - order is audible. On a sound layer, the
chain it runs over the mix.

id.description:
Minted by the editor ("c1", "c2", ...); how every command names its
target. Survives splits - the head keeps the id - and merges.

keys.description:
The user's own keys, sorted by property and then by `at`. Empty is a
clip whose properties are the constants above. A keyed property's
keys travel absolutely: they replace the constant rather than ride
on it.

kind.description:
What this clip renders as. Follows the media's kind, and is rewritten
when a template slot is filled with a different kind of file.

masks.description: The shapes that keep part of the picture, top first; see [`Mask`].

mediaId.description: Empty for a text clip, which has no file behind it.

motion.description: How it comes on, goes off and moves in between; see [`ClipMotion`].

muted.description: True when a video clip's embedded audio is detached out of it.

name.description:
Display label. Snapshotted from the media's name (or a title's first
line) at creation, then the user's to change.

offsetX.description: Offset from centred, as a fraction of frame width / height.

offsetY.description: The vertical half of `offset_x`'s pair; positive moves down.

opacity.description: Blend strength over whatever is beneath, in 0..1.

preservePitch.description:
Keep voices at their natural pitch when `speed` is not 1. On by
default; off gives the tape-machine chipmunk/slow-motion sound.

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the picture's centre.

scale.description: Multiplier over the fitted size. 1 fills the frame, preserving aspect.

shape.description: The figure, when this is a shape clip.

sourceStart.description: In-point: how far into the media the clip starts.

speed.description:
Playback rate. 1 is normal. With a curve set this is the curve's
mean, kept in step by the commands that set either.

speedCurve.description:
Speed as it changes over the clip: points of `(at, speed)`, `at` a
fraction of the clip's timeline length. None is the constant rate.

stabilize.description: The camera's shake taken out; see [`Stabilize`]. None is off.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the timeline.

stretchX.description:
A multiplier on the fitted width beyond `scale`, for a picture
pulled wider or narrower than its aspect; 1 keeps the aspect.

text.description: The overlay, when this is a text clip.

trackId.description:
The lane this clip sits on. Always a track of the same timeline; the
reader drops clips whose track vanished.

transitionIn.description: The transition on the cut into this clip, if any.

videoEffects.description: Video effects, in order - the visual sibling of `filters`.

voice.description:
The voice in the clip's sound set apart from everything else, each
at a level of its own; see [`VoiceMix`]. None plays it as recorded.

ClipKey.description:
One user-set key: a property, a point in the clip, and the value there.

The value is *absolute* - the number the inspector shows, in the
property's own units - and not the relative factor the engine's
`animate::Key` carries. Storing what the user typed is what keeps a key
meaning the same thing after the clip's own scale or gain is changed
underneath it; the conversion to relative happens on the way out, in
`concat_export::flatten::export_keys`.

at.description: Where in the clip, as a fraction of its timeline length, `0..=1`.

ease.description: How this key is approached from the previous one.

value.description: The value there, in the property's own units.

ClipKind.description:
What a clip can be - wider than [`MediaKind`] because a text clip has no
file behind it; it *is* its own content.

oneOf.description: A cut of a video media item.
A cut of audio - either audio media or sound detached from a video.
A placed still.
A title. No media behind it; the content lives in [`Clip::text`].

A treatment over everything beneath it for as long as it runs - a
look or an effect placed as a layer. No media behind it; the chain
lives in [`Clip::video_effects`], its strength in [`Clip::opacity`]
and its ramps in the fades.

A treatment of the sound for as long as it runs: its chain, in
[`Clip::filters`], works on the mix of everything audible over its
span - a voice changer, a room or a telephone over the whole
soundtrack, not one clip of it. No media behind it; how much of the
treated sound replaces the untreated is [`Clip::opacity`], the
strength a picture layer has, and its ramps are the fades. A kind of
its own rather than a flag on [`ClipKind::Layer`], so it stays what
it is with its chain emptied, and a build that predates it leaves it
out as a clip it cannot play rather than reading it as a picture
layer that treats nothing.

A shape: a square, a circle, an arrow, drawn over the picture. No
media behind it; what it is and how it is painted lives in
[`Clip::shape`], and it is placed and scaled like a still.

A transition placed on the timeline as a clip of its own (#621),
acting on everything beneath it for as long as it runs: across a cut
under it, the outgoing picture into the incoming one, each carried
into the span by its own footage or a held frame; over a single
shot, the package played over that shot. No media behind it; the
package and its knobs are the one link in [`Clip::video_effects`],
and its length is the clip's. Unlike [`Clip::transition_in`], which
ties a transition to the cut into one clip, it is placed, moved and
trimmed like any clip.

ClipLoop.description:
A loop by name - `pulse`, `heartbeat`, `float`, `wiggle`, `sway`,
`jitter`, `spin`, `flicker`, `breathe` - a lap every `seconds`, at
`amount` (1 as designed).

amount.description: How much of it, 0 to 2; one when left out.

seconds.description: Seconds a lap takes; one when left out.

ClipMotion.description:
How a clip comes on, goes off and moves in between: an entrance, an
exit and a loop, any of them. Each is applied where the clip is placed,
over its keys, so the whole picture moves - a picture-in-picture slides
as a card, a title pops as a title. See `concat_core::motion` for what
each move does; a name the app does not know is kept and ignored.

ClipMove.description: Where one clip is going, in a multi-clip move.

clipId.description:
The clip to move. An unknown id is skipped, not an error - the rest
of the batch of moves still lands.

start.description: New timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description:
Destination track. An unknown id moves the clip in time but leaves it
on its current track.

ClipPatch.description:
A partial update to one clip. Every field optional; `transition_in` and
`text` are double-optional so "clear it" and "leave it alone" stay
distinct on the wire (absent = untouched, null = cleared).

audioStream.description:
Which of the media's audio streams the clip plays, by stream index:
absent leaves it alone, null goes back to the file's first, a value
names one. See `Clip::audio_stream`.

background.description:
The clip's own background over the timeline's: absent leaves it
alone, null goes back to following the timeline's, a value - black
included - is the clip's own. See `Clip::background`.

blend.description: The blend mode's name; empty is normal.

crop.description:
The crop, same three-way wire semantics as `transition_in`: absent
leaves it alone, null takes it off, a value replaces it.

fadeIn.description: New fade-in length in seconds, floored at 0.

fadeOut.description: New fade-out length in seconds, floored at 0.

filters.description:
Wholesale replacement of the audio filter chain - the UI sends the
full list, not a diff.

masks.description:
The masks, top first: absent leaves them alone, a list replaces
them, empty takes them all off. Tidied on the way in; an empty or
repeated id is minted anew. Each carries its own keys
(`setMaskKey`).

motion.description:
The entrance, exit and loop, same three-way wire semantics as
`crop`: absent leaves them alone, null takes them all off, a value
replaces them, tidied on the way in.

muted.description:
Whether the clip's own sound is silenced: true mutes it, false lets
it play again. A detach sets this on the video it took the sound
from, so this is also how a video whose detached sound was later
deleted gets its voice back.

name.description:
New display name, taken verbatim. A later `text` patch overwrites it
with the title's first line.

preservePitch.description: New pitch-preservation setting, taken as sent.

shape.description:
A shape clip's figure and paint, whole: absent leaves it alone. Only
a shape clip takes it.

text.description:
The title styling, same three-way wire semantics as `transition_in`.
Setting a style also renames the clip after its first line.

transitionIn.description:
The transition on the cut into the clip: absent leaves it alone,
null clears it, a value replaces it.

videoEffects.description: Wholesale replacement of the video effect chain, like `filters`.

volume.description:
New gain; floored at 0, deliberately not capped at 1 - boosting quiet
footage is legitimate.

ColorRange.description:
The levels a media file's picture spans, when the person says so over
whatever the file claims: video range, 16-235, or full range, 0-255.
A screen recording written full and tagged nothing plays grey where it
should be black until it is read as `full`; a video-range file tagged
full crushes its shadows until it is read as `limited`. Set with
`Command::SetMediaColorRange`; absent means the file's own tag is read.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/103

oneOf.description: 16-235: what broadcast, cameras and every player expect.
0-255: what screen recorders and some phones write.

ColorSpace.description:
The colour a picture is in: SDR on Rec. 709, or HDR on Rec. 2020 with
the hybrid log-gamma or the perceptual quantiser transfer. A timeline's
is what it is output in; a media file's, what it was recorded in.

oneOf.description: Rec. 709, SDR: every timeline until its first HDR clip.

Rec. 2020 with HLG: what an iPhone records, and what a timeline
becomes on its first HDR clip.
Rec. 2020 with PQ: HDR10.

Command.description:
Every edit, as the window sends it: a tagged `op` plus camelCase
fields. [`apply`] is the single place each variant's meaning lives; the
notes here state the contract - clamps, tolerances, what gets minted -
so a caller need not read `apply` to know what a command will do.

oneOf.description:
Imports a file into the bin, minting an "m" id. A path already
present is a tolerated no-op that mints nothing.

item.description: The probed file, as described by the host.

oneOf.description:
Removes a bin item and every clip referencing it, on *all* timelines
- a clip whose media is gone would linger as a dead reference.

mediaId.description: The bin item to remove. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Marks a bin item as a template slot (or back to ordinary media),
which is what [`Command::FillSlot`] requires of its target.

mediaId.description: The bin item to mark. An unknown id is a no-op.

placeholder.description: True to make it a slot, false to make it ordinary media again.

oneOf.description:
Swaps the user's file into a template slot in place. The slot keeps
its id so clips keep working; start, duration and speed stay the
template's, while the in-point resets and each clip's kind and name
follow the new file, across all timelines. Errs if the id is unknown
or the item is not a placeholder.

item.description: The user's file that takes the slot's place.

mediaId.description: The slot being filled - must have `placeholder` set.

oneOf.description:
Several commands as one atomic edit: applied to a staged copy and
committed only if every one succeeds, then recorded as a single undo
step. The outcome carries the last id minted inside.

commands.description: The commands, applied in order. Nesting is legal.

oneOf.description:
Places a clip of `media_id` on a named track, minting a "c" id.
Duration comes from the media (five seconds for a still or unknown
length); errs if the media or track no longer exists.

mediaId.description: The bin item to cut from.

ripple.description:
When true and the drop would overlap something on this track,
every clip at or after `start` is shifted right by the new
clip's duration, so the drop lands without covering anything.
False for programmatic adds, true for a drop from the bin.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description: The lane to place it on.

oneOf.description:
[`Command::AddClip`] without naming a lane: lands on the lowest
track with nothing in the clip's span, falling back to the bottom
track (overlap and all) rather than refusing.

mediaId.description: The bin item to cut from.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

oneOf.description:
Several bin items one after another on one lane, as one step: what
a selection of cards dragged from the bin, or added at the playhead,
lands as. Each clip starts where the one before it ends. Naming a
lane puts the run there, each clip placed as [`Command::AddClip`]
places one with the same `ripple`; without one, the run goes on the
lowest lane free for its whole length, a new one when none is.

mediaIds.description: The bin items, in the order they are laid down.

ripple.description:
On a named lane, make room as a drop does rather than take the
nearest gap.

start.description: Where the first clip starts, in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description: The lane, or None for the lowest one free for the whole run.

oneOf.description:
Places a title: a clip with no media behind it, named after the
text's first line, minting a "c" id.

above.description:
When `track_id` is None and this is true, the clip lands on the
first free lane *above* the highest one occupied over its span,
minting a new lane at the top when every one above is taken.
What the editor sets for a caption and for a title alike, so
words sit over the video rather than under it; false keeps the
bottom-first walk of [`Command::AddClipAtFirstFree`]. Ignored
when `track_id` names a track.

duration.description:
Seconds on the timeline; the editorial default when absent. Here
so a caption run can land as one batch instead of add-then-trim
per clip - a batch cannot trim a clip whose id it cannot know yet.

offsetY.description:
Vertical placement as a frame-height fraction, clamped like
SetClipTransform. Lower thirds are made of this.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

style.description: The words and their look. None means [`TextStyle::default`].

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on. None picks the first free track like
[`Command::AddClipAtFirstFree`]; naming a vanished track errs.

oneOf.description:
Places a shape: a clip with no media behind it that draws one
figure over the picture, minting a "c" id. Lands the way a title
does - above the picture - since a shape is drawn over it.

duration.description: Seconds on the timeline; the editorial default when absent.

name.description:
What the lane calls it: the figure's name in the interface's
language, which the document cannot know.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

style.description: The figure and its paint. None means [`ShapeStyle::default`].

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on; None picks a lane as `above` says, as
[`Command::AddTextClip`] does.

oneOf.description:
Places a layer: a look or an effect over a span of the timeline that
treats everything beneath it. No media; the chain starts as the one
package named, at its defaults, and the clip's opacity is how hard it
is applied. With `sound`, a sound layer: an audio package, run over
the mix of everything audible for its span.

duration.description: Seconds on the timeline; the editorial default when absent.

effectId.description:
The package the layer applies, e.g. "concat.warm", or an audio
one, e.g. "concat.telephone", with `sound`.

sound.description:
True lays a sound layer ([`crate::model::ClipKind::SoundLayer`]):
the package goes on the clip's `filters`, and the layer treats
the soundtrack rather than the picture. Absent is a picture
layer.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on. None picks the first free lane *above*
the highest one occupied over its span, minting one at the top
when every lane above is taken: a layer treats what is beneath
it, so one under the picture would treat nothing.

oneOf.description:
Places a transition as a clip of its own (#621): the package named,
at its defaults, acting on everything beneath it for its span - from
the outgoing picture into the incoming one across a cut under it,
or played over the one shot where there is no cut. See
[`crate::model::ClipKind::Transition`].

duration.description:
Seconds on the timeline; a second when absent, and never less
than [`crate::model::ranges::MIN_TRANSITION`].

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on. None picks the first free lane above
the highest one occupied over its span, as a layer does, minting
one at the top when every lane above is taken: a transition acts
on what is beneath it.

oneOf.description:
Gives a clip a speed curve, or takes it away. The source covered is
held constant, as a speed change does, so the clip's timeline length
follows the curve's mean; `speed` is kept at that mean.

curve.description:
The curve, or None for a constant rate at the current mean.
Its points are put in order of `at`, held to `0..=1` and to the
speed range, and reach both ends of the clip, as they will be
played and saved. A curve with no usable point is None.

ripple.description:
The magnetic timeline: the clips behind on the lane follow the
clip's end whether it grows or shrinks, closing up the gap a
shrink would leave. False moves them only to make room when the
clip grows over the next.

oneOf.description:
Puts a key on one property at one point of a clip, replacing
whichever key on that property was already within a hair of it.

The value is the property's own - the number the inspector shows -
not the relative factor the engine plays; see `model::ClipKey`.

ease.description: How the key is approached from the one before it.

oneOf.description:
Takes the key at `at` off one property, if there is one there. The
other half of the diamond: a filled diamond clicked is this.

at.description: Where in the clip the key to remove sits, `0..=1`.

oneOf.description: Takes every key off one property, returning it to its constant.

Puts a key on one parameter of one link of a clip's picture chain,
replacing whichever key on it was already within a hair of `at`.
The value is the parameter's own; the package's range is the
caller's to keep, the model not knowing it.

ease.description: How the key is approached from the one before it.

entry.description:
Which link, as an index into `video_effects`. Out of range is a
no-op.

oneOf.description: Takes the key at `at` off one parameter of one link, if there is one.

at.description: Where in the clip the key to remove sits, `0..=1`.

entry.description: Which link, as an index into `video_effects`.

oneOf.description:
Takes every key off one parameter of one link, returning it to the
value it holds.

entry.description: Which link, as an index into `video_effects`.

oneOf.description:
Puts a key on one number of one of a clip's masks, replacing
whichever key on it was already within a hair of `at`. The value is
the number's own, held to its range.

ease.description: How the key is approached from the one before it.

maskId.description: The mask's id. One the clip does not have is a no-op.

oneOf.description: Takes the key at `at` off one number of one mask, if there is one.

at.description: Where in the clip the key to remove sits, `0..=1`.

oneOf.description:
Takes every key off one number of one mask, returning it to the
value it holds.

Sets or clears a picture's cutout: the mask that takes its
background away. Tidied on the way in; see [`Cutout::tidy`].

clipId.description: The clip. An unknown id is a no-op.

cutout.description: The cutout, or None to take it off.

oneOf.description:
Turns a picture's stabilization on, sets its settings, or takes it
off. Tidied on the way in; see [`Stabilize::tidy`]. The camera's
movement is measured by the host the first time a clip of the
media asks for it; until then the clip shows as shot.

clipId.description: The clip. An unknown id is a no-op.

stabilize.description: The settings, or None to take stabilization off.

oneOf.description:
Sets a clip's voice isolation - the voice and the rest at levels of
their own - or takes it off. Tidied on the way in; see
[`VoiceMix::tidy`]. A clip with no sound is left as it is. The two
parts are worked out by the host the first time a clip of the media
asks for them; until then the clip plays as recorded.

clipId.description: The clip. An unknown id is a no-op.

voice.description: The levels, or None to play the clip as recorded.

oneOf.description:
Paints one stroke onto a clip's cutout. A clip with no cutout gets a
custom one; an automatic cutout becomes custom, since a stroke is a
correction to it. A stroke with no points is a no-op.

clipId.description: The clip. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Repositions any number of clips in one edit - one undo step for a
whole multi-selection drag. Unknown clips and tracks are tolerated
per [`ClipMove`].

Drags one edge of a clip. A head trim moves the in-point with the
edge (scaled by speed) so the remaining pixels do not slide; either
edge stops at the sixtieth-of-a-second minimum duration. An unknown
clip is a no-op.

delta.description:
Signed seconds of timeline the edge moves: positive drags the
head right (shortening) or the tail right (lengthening).

ripple.description:
When true the lane closes up behind the trim - the magnetic
timeline. A tail trim moves every later clip on the track by
the change in length. A head trim keeps the clip where it was
(the in-point moves, the start does not) and moves every later
clip by what was cut or restored, so the trimmed clip and the
one behind it stay touching. False trims the clip alone.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/106

oneOf.description:
Cuts each named clip in two at one playhead time. The head keeps the
id and the transition; the tail is minted fresh and stays
source-continuous. A clip the time misses (or grazes within the
minimum duration) is skipped.

clipIds.description: The clips under the playhead - normally the selection.

time.description: The cut point, in timeline seconds.

oneOf.description:
Points a clip at another file - the enhanced or reversed copy of
its media - adding the file to the bin first when it is not there.
The clip's length, looks and name are kept, and its in-point unless
`source_start` moves it: an enhanced copy stands in for the original
frame for frame, a reversed one covers the span the clip showed and
starts at its own zero. The bin keeps the original, since other
clips may show it and undo may want it back. An unknown clip is a
no-op.

enhanced.description:
The copy is the clip's Enhance: the clip keeps the media it
showed before as the original, so Enhance can be switched off
(see [`Command::SetClipEnhanced`]). Any other copy - a reversed
one - ends the clip's Enhance, which was of the media now gone.

item.description: The probed copy, as described by the host.

offset.description:
With `enhanced`, the seconds into the original the copy starts
at (see [`crate::model::Enhanced::offset`]); `source_start` is
then the clip's in-point in the copy.

sourceStart.description:
A new in-point in the copy, in seconds, floored at 0. Absent
keeps the clip's.

oneOf.description:
Shows a clip's enhanced copy, or its original again. A no-op for a
clip Enhance has not made a copy for.

on.description: The copy when true, the original when false.

oneOf.description:
A freeze frame at `time`: splits `clip_id`, inserts a still of
`duration` on the same track, and ripples later clips on that track
by `duration`. Video needs a probed `still` (host-extracted jpg);
image clips may omit it and reuse their media. Audio and text are
no-ops. `created_id` is the freeze clip.

clipId.description: The picture clip under the playhead.

duration.description:
Editorial length of the hold. Floored at [`MIN_CLIP_DURATION`];
when absent or non-positive, uses [`DEFAULT_FREEZE_DURATION`].

still.description:
Probed still file. Required for video; ignored for image when
reusing the existing media.

time.description: Timeline playhead; must fall strictly inside the clip.

oneOf.description:
Rejoins split pieces into the earliest piece, which keeps its id.
Errs with a user-facing sentence ([`why_not_merge`]) unless the
pieces sit on one track, come from one file at one speed, touch
within a microsecond, and are still in source order.

clipIds.description: The pieces to rejoin, any order.
Two or more video clips on one track, in any order.

item.description: The completed, probed render stored in the project media folder.

oneOf.description: Deletes clips from the active timeline. Unknown ids are ignored.

ripple.description:
When true the deletion leaves no gap: on each track, every clip
that starts after a removed span moves left by the length of the
removed spans before it. A track the deletion never touched
stays where it is, so a picture going from one lane does not
pull the sound on another - the magnetic track, which is
what was asked for. False leaves the hole.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/106

oneOf.description:
Applies a [`ClipPatch`]: only the fields present change, with the
clamps documented on the patch. An unknown clip is a no-op.

patch.description: Which properties change, and to what.

oneOf.description:
Gives some of a title's words a look of their own: each field of
`patch` is laid over the characters `start..end` of its words, and
each it leaves out stays as it was there - the title's own look, or
what an earlier run gave them. `start` and `end` count characters
(Unicode scalar values), not bytes, and are clamped to the words; an
empty range, an empty patch, a clip that is not a title or an
unknown clip is a no-op. The title's own style is untouched, so the
words left out keep following it. See `TextStyle::runs`.

patch.description: The overrides to lay over them.

oneOf.description:
Gives a title's words back to its own look: every run is cut out of
the characters `start..end`, or out of all of them when either end
is absent. Counted and clamped as in `styleTextRange`; a clip that
is not a title or an unknown clip is a no-op.

end.description: One past the last, absent for the end of the words.

start.description: The first character, absent for the start of the words.

oneOf.description:
Changes playback rate while holding the amount of source covered
constant - the clip's timeline duration is what stretches, which is
what makes this a speed change rather than a trim.

clipId.description: The clip to retime. An unknown id is a no-op.

ripple.description:
The magnetic timeline: the clips behind on the lane follow the
clip's end whether it grows or shrinks, closing up the gap a
shrink would leave. False moves them only to make room when the
clip grows over the next.

speed.description:
The new rate, clamped into 0.0625..=16 (the engine's range).
A speed curve the clip had ends: the footage it covered is kept.

oneOf.description:
Adjusts the picture's placement. Each field is optional so a drag
can send just the axis it moved; absent fields stay put.

clipId.description: The clip to place. An unknown id is a no-op.

offsetX.description: New horizontal offset as a frame-width fraction, clamped to ±3.

offsetY.description: New vertical offset as a frame-height fraction, clamped to ±3.

rotation.description:
New rotation in degrees, wrapped into (-180, 180] so a full drag
never accumulates turns.

stretchX.description: New width multiplier beyond the scale, clamped into 0.1..=10.

stretchY.description: New height multiplier, on the same terms.

oneOf.description:
Sizes a picture to the frame in one step: fitted whole inside it,
or covering it, centred either way and unstretched (see
[`crate::model::framing_scale`]; a turned picture is sized as turned).
A scale or a position with keys gets a key at `at` rather than a new
constant, the way every edit of a keyed property lands, so the rest
of the ride is left as it was. A no-op for a clip that is not a video
or a still, or whose media's size is unknown.

at.description: Where in the clip, `0..=1`, a keyed property takes its key.

clipId.description: The clip to size. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Pulls a video clip's sound out into its own audio clip on a free
lane (minting one if none is free), muting the video and moving its
audio filters to the sound. A no-op unless the clip is an unmuted
video whose media has audio and is not already detached.

clipId.description: The video clip to detach from.

oneOf.description:
Undoes a detach: deletes the detached sound clip(s), unmutes the
video and hands the sound's filters back. Accepts either the video's
id or the sound's; a no-op when either side is gone.

clipId.description: The video clip - or its detached sound.

oneOf.description:
Adds a lane, minting a "t" id: on top of the stack, or with
`bottom` under every other lane. Absent is the top, which is what
the command did before it could do anything else.

bottom.description: Under every other lane rather than on top of them.

oneOf.description: Deletes a lane and every clip on it. Errs at the floor of one track.
Flips one of a track's two toggles. An unknown id is a no-op.

Adds a fresh timeline - four new lanes, "Timeline N" after the
highest in use - and makes it active. Mints a "tl" id.

Deletes a timeline, moving the active tab to a neighbour if it was
this one. Errs at the floor of one timeline.

timelineId.description: The timeline to delete. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Sets a timeline's output frame and rate. A term no frame could have,
such as a zero dimension or a zero rate, is refused as a no-op rather
than clamped: there is no nearest real size to a zero.

timelineId.description: The timeline. An unknown id is a no-op.

video.description: The frame and the rate, together.

oneOf.description:
Sets what fills a timeline's frame behind the pictures on its lowest
picture lane; see `Timeline::background_of`. Tidied first: an amount
held to `0..=1`, a colour that does not read made black.

timelineId.description: The timeline. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Turns a timeline's linkage on or off: whether its other lanes follow
an edit that closes up or opens its main lane. See
`Timeline::linkage`.

on.description: On: the other lanes follow the main one.

timelineId.description: The timeline. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Renames a timeline tab. Whitespace-only names are ignored so a tab
can never end up blank; unknown ids are tolerated.

name.description: The new tab label; trimmed before it lands.

oneOf.description:
Switches which timeline subsequent commands act on. An unknown id
leaves the selection where it was.

Moves a timeline tab to a new position in the strip. Which timeline
is active does not change - only the order of the tabs.

index.description:
Where it lands among its siblings, 0-based, counted with the
timeline already removed from its old slot. Clamped to the end.

timelineId.description: The timeline to move. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
Registers a font file for titles. A path already registered is a
no-op, so re-adding cannot duplicate.

family.description: The family name titles will refer to.

path.description: Where the font file lives on disk.

oneOf.description:
Unregisters a font family. Clips keep the family name: the face may
come back when the file does.
Updates a media item's path on disk (relink). An unknown id is a no-op.

newPath.description: The new absolute path on disk.

oneOf.description:
Says what levels a media file's picture really spans, over whatever
the file claims: the fix for a screen recording written full range
and tagged nothing, which plays grey where it should be black, or a
video-range file tagged full, which crushes its shadows. Reaches
every clip of the media, on every timeline, in the monitor and the
export alike. An unknown id is a no-op.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/103

range.description:
`limited` or `full`, or None to go back to reading the file's

CustomFont.description: A font the user added from disk.

family.description:
The family name titles refer to; removal leaves referring clips
untouched so the face can come back when the file does.

path.description:
Where the font file lives on disk. Doubles as the duplicate check
when adding.

Cutout.description:
How a picture's background is taken away when there is no key colour
to remove: a person mask found by the cutout model, alone or corrected
by hand.

feather.description: How far the edge is softened, as a fraction of the picture's width.

mode.description: Automatic keeps what the model finds; custom adds the strokes.

strokes.description: Corrections painted on the monitor, in the order they were made.

CutoutMode.description: The two ways a cutout decides what stays.

oneOf.description: The model's mask as it is.
The model's mask, then the strokes over it.

data.description: Large state: downloaded models, painted titles.

Done.description: The empty reply, an object so every reply is one.

EditorView.description:
What every mutating call returns: the authoritative state plus history
availability, so undo/redo affordances are never guessing.

canRedo.description: Whether there is something to redo.

canUndo.description: Whether there is something to undo.

createdId.description: The id a creating command minted, if any.

project.description: The whole project, as the engine holds it.

settings.description:
The settings as the session holds them - the document's own output
size wins over the manifest's on open.

Enhanced.description: A clip's Enhance, once it has a copy: see [`Clip::enhanced`].

copy.description: The bin item holding the enhanced copy.

offset.description:
Seconds into the original the copy starts at: a copy of the span the
clip covers, rather than of the whole file, starts partway in. The
clip's in-point is in the copy's seconds while it shows the copy, so
switching between the two moves it by this much and the same moment
stays on screen. Zero, and left out of the document, for a copy of
the whole file.

on.description: Whether the clip shows the copy.

original.description: The bin item the clip was cut from.

ErrorCode.description:
Why a request has no reply, as a program reads it. The JSON-RPC number
each maps to is [`ErrorCode::number`].

oneOf.description: The line was not JSON.

The JSON was not a request: an unknown method, a missing or
ill-typed field, a value out of range.
The project named is not open; open it first.

would show, and the state is as it was.

The transport wanted a token and did not get the right one. Never

Everything else: a file that could not be read or written, a decode

Event.description:
Something that happened to a job. A transport forwards these to every
caller as they come; each names its job and its project, so a caller
keeps the ones it asked for and ignores the rest.

oneOf.description: A cutout's masks are being found ahead of an export.

fetching.description: True while a model downloads, false while it runs.

oneOf.description: A stabilized clip's media is being measured ahead of an export.
The export moved on.
The export wrote its file. The job is over.
The export did not write its file. The job is over.

error.description:
Why: [`ErrorCode::Cancelled`] when asked to stop, otherwise what
went wrong.

Fill.description: One template slot and the file that takes it.

file.description: The file to put there; probed on the way in.

mediaId.description: The placeholder's media id in the template.

Framing.description: The two ways a picture can be sized to the frame in one go.

oneOf.description:
The whole picture in the frame, as large as it goes: bars where the
shapes differ. Every picture's size before it is touched.

The frame covered, the picture centred and cut at the edges that
overhang it.

JobState.description: Where a job is in its life.

oneOf.description: Still working.
Wrote its file.
Stopped by [`Request::ExportCancel`].
Ended without its file; `error` says why.

error.description: Why it failed, or that it was cancelled.

fraction.description: How far along the current stage is, `0..=1`; 1 once done.

frame.description: Frames rendered, in the video stage.

height.description: The written file's picture size, once done.

stage.description:
What it is doing: "cutout" while masks are found, "stabilize" while
shake is measured, then "rendering", "mixing audio" and "muxing";
"rendering in software" when the hardware encoder stopped part way
and the video is rendered again from its first frame on the CPU.
Absent until it has said.

total.description: Frames in all, in the video stage; 0 until known.

width.description: The written file's picture size, once done.

KeyEase.description:
How a key is approached from the one before it: a CSS timing function's
two control points, `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`.

The document's spelling of `concat_core::animate::Ease`, which is what it
becomes. Four numbers rather than a named shape because the curve editor
hands people a bezier to drag and the four named shapes are only its
preset chips - see `KeyEase::LINEAR` and friends.

Serialised as a bare array: `"ease": [0.42, 0, 0.58, 1]`. Documents
written before the curve editor spell it `"linear"` / `"in"` / `"out"` /
`"inOut"` instead, and `from_value` still reads those.

KeyProperty.description:
Which property a user-set key belongs to.

Five of the first six are the picture's placement and the sixth is the
mix's; the seven after them are the mask's numbers. They are one
enum because a key is a key - the panel that sets them, the commands that
carry them and the document that stores them do not care which side of
the clip a value ends up on, and only the thing that finally reads them
does.

oneOf.description: `Clip::scale`.
`Clip::offset_x`.
`Clip::offset_y`.
`Clip::rotation`.
`Clip::opacity`.
`Clip::volume`.

LineHead.description: What a line wears on an end.

oneOf.description: The line's own round end.
Two strokes, open.
A filled point.
A filled dot.
A short bar across.

Mask.description:
One of a clip's masks: a shape that keeps part of its picture, takes
part away, or - set to cut nothing - waits for a layer or an effect to
use it. Drawn over the picture as it is seen - after the crop and the
flips, before the placement - so it moves, scales and turns with the
clip, and multiplies with the cutout's matte and everything else that
weighs the picture.

A mask is its own: its keys are in [`Mask::keys`], not the clip's, so
one taken to another clip takes its animation with it, and a tracker
writes its path there.

expand.description:
How far the edge is moved out, in the picture's shorter side; in
when negative.

feather.description:
How soft the edge is, `0..=1`: one fades across half the picture's
shorter side.

id.description:
Unique among the clip's masks; what a layer or an effect that uses
it names it by. Left out, one is minted.

invert.description: Keeps the outside of the shape instead of the inside.

keys.description:
The numbers that ride rather than hold, by [`Mask::NUMBERS`] name,
each `at` a fraction of the clip like a `ClipKey`'s. A number with
keys is played from them, and the field above is only what it falls
back to with the keys taken off.

mode.description: How it joins the masks above it.

name.description: What the panel calls it; empty for the panel's own numbering.

rotation.description: Clockwise degrees about the mask's centre.

scale.description: A factor on its size, both ways.

source.description: What it is drawn from. Left out, a circle.

x.description:
The centre's offset from the picture's centre, as a fraction of the
picture's width; positive is right.

y.description: The same down the picture's height; positive is down.

MaskMode.description:
How a mask joins the masks above it in its clip's list. The names are
written into project files, so they are stable for ever. See
`concat_core::mask::MaskMode` for what each does.

oneOf.description: Keeps what it covers as well: the default.
Takes away what it covers.
Keeps only what it and the masks above it share.
Cuts nothing: kept for a layer or an effect to use.

MaskShape.description:
Which shape a clip's mask keeps. The names are written into project
files, so they are stable for ever.

oneOf.description: The part of the picture on one side of a line through the centre.
A band along a line through the centre: the line mirrored.

An ellipse; a circle when its box is square. The default, and what
the reader falls back to.
A box, its corners rounded by the mask's `roundness`.
A heart, point down.
A five-pointed star, point up.

MaskSource.description:
What a mask is drawn from. One kind today; the pen's outline and the
subject a click picks join it, each with its own numbers.

oneOf.description:
A shape in a box: a line, a band, an ellipse, a box, a heart, a
star.

height.description: The box's height on the same terms; a band's thickness.

roundness.description: How round a box's corners are, `0..=1`.

width.description:
The box's width, in the picture's shorter side - the unit that
keeps a circle round on any aspect - before the mask's scale.
Left out, a new mask of the shape's.

MediaItem.description:
One entry in the media bin: a file the user imported, plus what the host's
probe learned about it. The probe metadata is stored, not re-derived, so a
document opens meaningfully even when the file itself is missing.

audioCodec.description: Codec of the embedded audio, when there is any.

audioTracks.description:
Every audio stream the file carries, in file order, when the probe
listed them. Empty for a file without sound and for a document from
before the list was kept - `has_audio` still says whether there is
sound at all. More than one is a recording with its tracks apart, and
what lets a clip choose between them. Skipped when empty, so
documents without such media stay byte-identical.

colorRange.description:
The levels the picture is read as, over the file's own tag; see
[`ColorRange`]. Absent, and left out of the document, for the tag.

colorSpace.description:
What the probe found the picture recorded in: HLG or PQ for HDR.
Left out of the document for SDR - and absent from one written
before it was kept, which reads as SDR.

duration.description: Seconds. None when the container did not say.

frameRate.description: Frames per second as a decimal - convenient for display, not exact.

frameRateFraction.description: The exact fraction the engine works in, e.g. "30000/1001".

hasAudio.description: Whether the file carries an audio stream; gates `DetachAudio`.

id.description:
Minted by the editor ("m1", "m2", ...) and never re-issued, even
across a save/load - clips reference media by this id.

kind.description:
What the probe decided the file is; fixes which [`ClipKind`] its
clips get.

name.description: Display name in the bin, normally the file's basename.

origin.description:
Where the file came from when the editor made it; see
[`MediaOrigin`]. Absent, and left out of the document, for an
import, and read as absent when it names an origin this build does
not know - the file is still a file, just one shelved with the
imports.

path.description:
Absolute path on the user's disk. Doubles as the duplicate check:
adding the same path twice is a no-op.

placeholder.description:
True when this item is a template slot: a stand-in whose metadata says
what kind of media belongs here, waiting to be replaced by the user's
own file (`Command::FillSlot`). In a creator's own project the path is
still real; only a packed template bundle blanks it. Skipped when
false, so documents without templates stay byte-identical.

videoCodec.description: Codec name as the probe reported it, e.g. "h264". Informational.

width.description: Pixel width, when the file has pictures and the probe found one.

MediaKind.description:
What a piece of media is. A still is not a video with one frame: it has no
intrinsic duration, so its length on a timeline is editorial.

oneOf.description: Moving pictures, with or without embedded sound.
Sound only; nothing to composite.
A still, whose timeline length is editorial rather than intrinsic.

MediaOrigin.description:
What made a media file, when it was the editor and not the user's
import. The bin shelves such a file under Generated, by origin, and
keeps it out of the import shelves.

oneOf.description: Read aloud by the speech sheet.

A clip's sound rendered as it played - trimmed, at its speed, with
its level, fades and effects baked in - as a file of its own.

audio.description:
The first audio stream in file order, if any: what a clip plays
unless it names another.

audioTracks.description: Every audio stream, in file order.

duration.description: Container duration in seconds, when the container states one.

An entrance or an exit: a move by name - `fade`, `slide-left`,

`drop`, `rise`, `spin`, `flip`, `swing`, `squash` - over `seconds`.

seconds.description: Seconds it takes; half a second when left out.

NewMedia.description: A media item as probed by the host, before the model mints its id.

audioCodec.description: Codec of the embedded audio, when there is any.

audioTracks.description:
Every audio stream, in file order; see `MediaItem::audio_tracks`.

colorSpace.description:
What the probe found the picture recorded in; see

Seconds, or None when the container did not report one - clips of

frameRate.description: Frames per second as a decimal, for display.

frameRateFraction.description: The exact rate fraction the engine works in, e.g. "30000/1001".

hasAudio.description: Whether the file carries an audio stream.

name.description: Display name for the bin, normally the file's basename.

origin.description:
What made the file, when the editor did; see `MediaItem::origin`.

path.description:
Absolute path on disk. Adding a path already in the bin is a no-op,

videoCodec.description: Codec name as probed, e.g. "h264". Informational.

width.description: Pixel width, when the probe found one.

category.description: The shelf the card sits on.

animate.description: Whether the control can carry keyframes.

The edit: everything the document stores except the app-level settings

Which timeline commands act on. Maintained by the command layer, so

What shows where no picture covers the frame, for a project's first

tenBit.description: Ten bits a channel. Eight when absent.

width.description: Output width; the timeline's when absent.

oneOf.description:
Stops a running export at its next frame. The job then ends with
[`Event::ExportFailed`] carrying [`ErrorCode::Cancelled`].

How a job stands: running and how far along, or how it ended. The
same news the events carry, for a caller that was not listening
when it came; the last few finished jobs are remembered.

Composites the true frame at one instant. Written as a PNG to
`output` when there is one, and handed back inline as a
[`Picture`] otherwise, for a caller on the far side of a socket.

height.description: Frame height; the timeline's when absent.

output.description: The file to write; absent means the picture comes back inline.

width.description: Frame width; the timeline's when absent.

RunStyle.description:
What a stretch of a title's words wears over the title's own look: each
field is an override, and one left out is the title's. Every word of a
title is the title's style until a run says otherwise, so a title with
no runs is exactly the title it always was.

color.description: Fill colour as `#rrggbb`, over the title's `color`.

fontScale.description:
Size as a multiple of the title's `fontSize`, 0.1..=10: 1.5 is half
as big again. Relative, not a size of its own, so a word made bigger
stays bigger by as much when the whole title is resized.

fontWeight.description:
CSS-scale weight, 100..=900, over the title's `fontWeight`; bold is
700, regular 400.

italic.description: Italic or upright, over the title's `italic`.

strikethrough.description: Struck through or not, over the title's `strikethrough`.

strokeColor.description:
Outline colour, over the title's `strokeColor`; shows where the
title has an outline at all.

underline.description: Underlined or not, over the title's `underline`.

SettingsView.description: The session's settings, as the window shows them.

ShapeGradient.description:
How a shape's inside is coloured past its one colour: a blend from
`fill` into a second colour.

angle.description:
Which way a straight blend runs, in degrees: 0 left to right, 90
top to bottom.

color.description: The colour the blend ends in, `#rrggbb[aa]`.

radial.description: Straight across at `angle`, or out from the middle.

ShapeKind.description:
Which figure a shape clip draws. The names are written into project
files, so they are stable for ever.

oneOf.description:
A rectangle: square until it is given a height of its own, with
corners as round as `corner_radius` says. The default, and what the
reader falls back to.
An ellipse: a disc until it is given a height of its own.
Point up, its base the box's bottom.
A slanted rectangle, leaning right.
A rectangle narrower at the top.

A straight stroke `stroke_width` thick, with what `start_head` and
`end_head` put on its ends.
A line whose end wears an arrowhead unless told otherwise.
A regular polygon of `sides` sides, a point up.

A star of `points` points, its inner corners `inner_radius` of the
way out.
A heart.

ShapeShadow.description:
A shadow under a shape - or, with no distance and a bright colour, a
glow around it.

angle.description: Which way it falls, in degrees: 90 straight down.

blur.description: How soft, as a fraction of frame height.

color.description: `#rrggbb[aa]`; its alpha is the shadow's strength.

distance.description: How far from the shape, as a fraction of frame height.

ShapeStyle.description:
How a shape clip is painted. Sizes are fractions of the frame's height,
as a title's are, so a shape composed against 1080p is the same shape at
4K. A style arriving in a command needs only the fields it changes.

cornerRadius.description:
How round a figure's corners are, 0 sharp to 1 as round as the
shorter side allows. Every figure with corners takes it.

dash.description: The outline's pattern; a line's too.

endHead.description:
What a line's end wears; None is the kind's own: an arrowhead on
an arrow, nothing on a line.

fill.description: The inside's colour as `#rrggbb[aa]`; empty for an outline alone.

gradient.description:
The inside blended from `fill` into a second colour, or None for
`fill` alone.

height.description:
The figure's height as a fraction of frame height; zero - the
default - is the figure's own proportion of its width (see
[`ShapeKind::natural_height`]). A line has no height of its own.

innerRadius.description:
How far out a star's inner corners sit, as a share of its outer
radius: low is spiky, high is nearly round.

shadow.description: A shadow or a glow, or None.

startHead.description: What a line's start wears; None is the kind's own: nothing.

stroke.description:
The outline's colour, drawn when `stroke_width` is above zero. A
line and an arrow are all stroke, drawn in this colour, and fall
back to `fill` when it is empty.

strokeAlign.description: Where the outline sits on the edge.

strokeWidth.description:
The outline's thickness as a fraction of frame height; zero for a
figure with no outline. A line's and an arrow's own thickness.

trimStart.description:
The outline drawn from `trim_start` to `trim_end` of the way round,
0 to 1: a ring part-drawn, a progress arc, a line partway along.

width.description:
The figure's width, or a line's length, as a fraction of frame
height. `size` is what documents before a height called it.

SlotInfo.description: One placeholder the user's media will replace.

kind.description: What kind of media the slot wants.

mediaId.description: The placeholder media's id in the template document.

name.description: The placeholder's name, as the creator labelled it.

seconds.description: Timeline seconds this slot covers, summed over its clips.

SpeedPoint.description: One point of a speed curve.

at.description: Where in the clip, as a fraction of its timeline length, 0..=1.

slope.description:
How fast the speed is changing there, in speed per unit of `at`.
When every point of a curve has one, the curve bends smoothly
through its points; when any lacks one, it runs in straight lines.

speed.description: Source seconds per timeline second there.

Stabilize.description:
A clip's stabilization: the camera's shake taken out of the picture.

The camera's movement is measured once, frame to frame, by the host's
analysis and cached in the project folder beside the masks; these are
the settings the smooth path and the correction are worked out from,
live, whenever they change. Off is no `Stabilize` at all.

keepRotation.description:
Leave the camera's roll as shot: only its drift and its zoom are
corrected.

maxZoom.description:
The most the picture may be zoomed to hide the edges the correction
moves into view, `1..=MAX_STABILIZE_ZOOM`. The zoom used is the
least the whole clip needs, up to this; past it the correction is
eased where it would show an edge.

smoothness.description:
How much of the camera's movement is smoothed away, `0..=1`: low
keeps a pan or a glide and takes out the jitter, high leaves only
the slowest of moves. Measured on the timeline, so a clip sped up
is smoothed as calmly as one at its own pace.

tripod.description:
Lock the frame entirely, as on a tripod, rather than follow the
camera's intended move.

Started.description: A job the API has begun. Every event about it carries `job`.

job.description: The job's name, unique for the life of the API: "j1", "j2", ...

Stroke.description:
One brush stroke over a cutout: which tool, how wide, and where it went.
Points are fractions of the source picture, `(0, 0)` its top-left, so a
stroke survives a change of output size, a crop or a flip.

at.description:
The source instant, in seconds, the stroke was painted at: the
frame a smart brush reads the thing under it from. Absent on
strokes from before it was recorded, which paint as plain discs.

size.description: The brush's diameter as a fraction of the picture's width.

tool.description: What the stroke does to the mask beneath it.

StrokeAlign.description: Where an outline sits on a figure's edge.

oneOf.description: Straddling the edge, half in and half out.
All inside the edge: the figure keeps its size.
All outside it: the fill keeps its size and the outline adds to it.
Unbroken.
Dashes three strokes long with two strokes between.
Round dots a stroke apart.

Subject.description:
What a cutout keeps: the person the matting model finds, the one
thing the picture is of whatever it is, or whichever of those the
analysis decides fits the footage.

oneOf.description: A person when the person model finds one, the object otherwise.
The person model, always.
The object model, always.

TemplateInfo.description: One template, as the gallery sees it.

hasPoster.description: Whether the bundle carries a poster.

slots.description: The slots to fill, in the order they first appear on the timeline.

TextAlign.description:
How a title's lines sit within their block, and which point of the block
the clip's position pins: a centred title is placed by its middle, a
left-aligned one by its block's left edge and a right-aligned one by its
right edge. Typing more into a left-aligned title grows it to the right
and leaves its left edge where it was, as alignment means everywhere.

oneOf.description: Lines share a left edge, which is where the clip's position is.

Lines are centred on each other and on the clip's position - the
default, and what the reader falls back to for an unrecognised value.
Lines share a right edge, which is where the clip's position is.

TextCase.description: Display casing, independent of the editable source text.

oneOf.description: Display all cased letters in uppercase.
Display all cased letters in lowercase.
Lowercase the text and capitalize sentence initials.
Preserve the editable source's capitalization.

TextRun.description:
A stretch of a title's words with a look of its own: some words in
another colour, one in bold. `start` and `end` count characters - Unicode
scalar values, what `str::chars` yields - into the title's `content`,
not bytes, so a caller in any language counts them the way it counts a
string; `end` is one past the last. Kept sorted, apart and non-empty;
see `TextStyle::style_range` and `TextStyle::edit_content`.

color.description: Fill colour as `#rrggbb`, over the title's `color`.

fontScale.description:
Size as a multiple of the title's `fontSize`, 0.1..=10: 1.5 is half
as big again. Relative, not a size of its own, so a word made bigger
stays bigger by as much when the whole title is resized.

fontWeight.description:
CSS-scale weight, 100..=900, over the title's `fontWeight`; bold is
700, regular 400.

italic.description: Italic or upright, over the title's `italic`.

start.description: The first character the look covers.

strikethrough.description: Struck through or not, over the title's `strikethrough`.

strokeColor.description:
Outline colour, over the title's `strokeColor`; shows where the
title has an outline at all.

underline.description: Underlined or not, over the title's `underline`.

TextStyle.description:
A title's styling. Sizes are fractions of the frame, so a title composed
against 1080p lands correctly exported at 4K. A style arriving in a
command needs only the fields it changes; the rest are the default's, so
a caller can say `{ "content": "Hello" }` and get a title that looks like
one the window would place.

align.description: Line alignment within the block; see [`TextAlign`].

background.description:
A solid background behind the text, `#rrggbb[aa]`; its alpha is the
background's opacity. Empty string for none. The painter and older
comments call it the plate.

backgroundPaddingX.description:
The air between the words and the background's left and right
edges, as a fraction of frame height, on an axis the words size
themselves: a box with a width is exactly that wide. The default
is the air every background had before it was a dial, 35 % of the
default size's em.

backgroundPaddingY.description: The same above and below; 20 % of the default em by default.

backgroundRadius.description:
The background's corner radius as a fraction of frame height, so a
title composed against 1080p keeps its corners at 4K. The default is
the rounding every background wore before it had a dial - 15 % of
the default size's em - and zero is square.

color.description: Fill colour as a CSS hex string, e.g. "#ffffff".

content.description:
The words themselves, newlines included. The clip's display name is
snapshotted from the first non-empty line.

fontFamily.description:
CSS-style family name, quotes included where the name needs them,
e.g. `"Hanken Grotesk"`. May name a [`CustomFont`] the user added.

fontSize.description: Cap height as a fraction of frame height.

fontWeight.description:
CSS-scale weight, 100..=900; the reader clamps hand-edited values
into that range.

italic.description: Italic when true. A style flag, not a separate face.

lineHeight.description:
Baseline spacing as a multiple of the font size; the reader floors it
at 0.5 so lines cannot collapse onto each other.

maxHeight.description:
The box's height as a fraction of frame height; the stage's top and
bottom grips set it, and the inspector's Height field. Zero - the
default - is the words' own height. With a height the block is a
box exactly that tall, the words centred in it, so a lower third
can be a band of a fixed size whatever is written on it.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/119

maxWidth.description:
The widest a line may run, as a fraction of frame width, before its
words wrap onto the next; the stage's side grips set it. Zero - the
default - is no limit: a line is as long as its words. With a limit
the block is a box exactly that wide, plate included, and the lines
align inside it.

opacity.description:
Opacity of the whole title in 0..=1, multiplied with the clip's own
opacity.

runs.description:
Stretches of the words with a look of their own over the rest of
this style - a word in another colour, in bold, bigger. Empty for a
title in one look, and then not written at all, so a document
without runs is the document it always was and an older build reads
a document with them as the title in its own look.

shadow.description: A drop shadow for legibility over footage. On by default.

strikethrough.description: Draw a strike through the text using the selected face's metrics.

strokeColor.description: Outline colour, only visible when `stroke_width` is non-zero.

strokeWidth.description:
Outline thickness as a fraction of frame height. Zero - the default -
means no stroke.

textCase.description: Case is applied for painting; the editable source stays intact.

tracking.description:
Extra letter spacing, in the same frame-height fractions as
`font_size`. Zero is the font's natural fit.

underline.description: Draw an underline using the selected face's metrics.

Timeline.description:
One timeline: a name and its lanes and clips. Every operation takes the
project and works on whichever timeline is active.

background.description:
What fills the frame behind the pictures on the lowest picture lane,
where they do not reach it; see [`Timeline::background_of`]. The
timeline's rather than [`VideoSettings`]' because that is the four
numbers a frame is, copied and compared everywhere, and this names
media. Black, and left out of the document, until one is chosen.

clips.description:
Every clip on this timeline, in insertion order, not time order -
readers must sort by `start` where order matters.

Behind `Arc` so that cloning the timeline - which undo does before
every command - copies one pointer per clip, and only the clip a
command then writes to is copied for real ([`Arc::make_mut`] in
[`Timeline::clip_mut`]). Reading through the `Arc` is transparent.

id.description: Minted by the editor ("tl2", ...), except the founding "TL1".

linkage.description:
Linkage: whether the other lanes follow an edit that closes up or
opens the main lane ([`Timeline::background_lane`]), so a caption,
a title, an overlay or a sound placed against the footage stays on
the frames it was placed against, as connected clips are in other
editors. On unless turned off, and left out of the document
while on.

name.description: The tab label; "Timeline N" by default, renameable but never blank.

tracks.description:
The lanes, top to bottom. Never empty - `RemoveTrack` keeps a floor
of one.

video.description:
The frame this timeline renders to and the rate it runs at. Each
timeline's own: a vertical cut for one platform and a wide one for
another are different frames of the same media, and that is most of
what a second timeline is for.

Track.description: A lane. Deliberately untyped: any media goes on any track.

id.description:
Minted per timeline ("t5", or "T1".."T4" for the first timeline's
starter lanes); never shared between timelines.

muted.description: Audio on this track is silent when true.

visible.description: Video clips on this track are left out of the composite when false.

oneOf.description: [`Track::visible`]: whether the track's video reaches the composite.
[`Track::muted`]: whether the track's audio is silenced.

Transition.description: A transition on the cut into a clip.

id.description: Which transition from the catalogue, e.g. "cross-fade".

params.description:
The package's knobs as set on this cut, by key; a knob left out is
at its default. Empty for every transition saved before knobs could
be set, which play exactly as they did.

TrimEdge.description:
Which end of a clip a trim drags. The two are not symmetric: see
[`Command::TrimClip`].

oneOf.description:
The head. Trimming here moves the in-point with the edge, so the
remaining frames stay where they were on the timeline.
The tail. Trimming here only lengthens or shortens the clip.

VersionInfo.description: The build and the contract it speaks.

capabilities.description:
What this build serves, as names a caller tests for membership:
what the API itself provides in every build, `events`, and what
only some builds do, `gpu` when frames composite on one; then what
the transport around it adds, `json-rpc`, `unix-socket` and `grpc`
for each of the socket transports listening. A name absent from
the list is not served, whatever the build; a name added later is
not a version bump, so a caller ignores names it does not know.

dirs.description: Where this machine keeps recents, templates and models.

VideoSettings.description:
A timeline's output frame, rate and colour.

The same four numbers the document's top-level `video` block has always
carried, now one set per timeline, and the colour it is output in. The
top-level block is still written, as the active timeline's frame and
rate, so a build that predates this reads the document it always did,
and a document from such a build gives every timeline that block on the
way in.

canvas.description:
What shows where no picture covers the frame - a gap, the space
around a title, a clip fading in - as straight `[r, g, b, a]`,
written `#rrggbb` in the document, or `#rrggbbaa` when it lets
something show through: opaque black unless the project was given
another (#456). Alpha zero is a transparent frame, for an overlay
exported in a format that keeps alpha; a format that does not
gets black there. Left out of the document while it is opaque
black, so those documents stay as they were.

colorSpace.description:
The colour the timeline is output in: SDR for every timeline from
before HDR, and until its first HDR clip (see
`Editor::follow_first_hdr`). Left out of the document for SDR, so
those documents stay as they were.

rateDen.description: Denominator of the frame rate, e.g. 1001 for 29.97 fps.

rateNum.description: Numerator of the frame rate, e.g. 30000 for 29.97 fps.

VideoStreamInfo.description: A video stream, as the UI sees it.

colorRange.description:
The levels the stream says its numbers span, "limited" or "full",
or absent when the file says nothing - which a player then takes
for limited.

colorSpace.description: What the picture was recorded in: HLG or PQ for HDR, absent for SDR.

frameRateFraction.description: The exact fraction the engine actually works in, e.g. "30000/1001".

VoiceKind.description: The two kinds of voice isolation, each its own model.

oneOf.description:
Singing apart from the music under it: a song's vocals and its
instrumental. Deezer's Spleeter, downloaded the first time.

Speech apart from the noise, the room and the music bed behind it:
dialogue cleaned. DeepFilterNet 3, shipped with the app. The
default: most of an edit's sound is people talking.

VoiceMix.description:
Voice isolation on a clip's sound: how loud the voice in it plays, and
how loud everything else does - music, noise, the room. Each is a gain,
`0..=MAX_VOICE_GAIN`, 1 as recorded; both at 1 is the clip as it was,
voice alone is a background of 0, and the voice taken out is a voice of
0. The two parts are worked out by the host the first time a clip of
the media asks for them; until then the clip plays as recorded.

background.description: The gain of everything but the voice.

kind.description:
What the voice is set apart from: a song's music, or a recording's
noise.

preview.frame.description: The file written when the request names an `output`; the picture itself when it does not.

project.document.description: The `concat.json` a save would write, as it stands.
